data.gender_notes: Violanda is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin 'Viola' meaning 'strength' and 'Andro' meaning 'man', Violanda symbolizes female strength in battle, especially against spiritual adversity. The name Violanda carries the meaning “Strength in Battle” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Violanda usually hope their child will grow to embody strength in battle and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Violanda total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

in_greek.name: Βιολάνδα
in_greek.meaning: γυναίκα του Θεού, ισχυρή και δυνατή
in_greek.long_meaning: Ο όνομα Βιολάνδα προέρχεται από τις λέξεις βίος (ζωή) και άνδράς (άνδρας). Είναι ένα ελληνικό όνομα που σημαίνει γυναίκα του Θεού, ισχυρή και δυνατή. Η Βιολάνδα είναι ένα όνομα που συνδέεται με την πίστη και την πνευματικότητα. Ο Θεός ενσάρκωσε τον άνθρωπο μέσω της ανδρικής μορφής και της ζωής του. Η Βιολάνδα είναι ένα όνομα που μνημονεύει την ενσάρκωση του Θεού και την δική του δύναμη

in_latin.name: Violanda
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Violanda a verbis vita et vir derivatur. Mulier Dei fortis et robusta appellatur. In ecclesia antiqua Violanda nomen nobilitatis et virtutis denotabat. Mulier Dei potestatem ac virtutem signabat. Nomen Violanda Christi Ecclesiam repraesentabat

in_english.long_meaning: The name Violanda is derived from the Hebrew words 'vi' (son of) and 'el' (God) and 'nada' ( strength). It means daughter of God, strong and powerful woman. In the biblical context, the name Violanda is associated with the figure of the woman who is a symbol of strength and power. In Christian tradition, the name Violanda is also associated with the virtues of courage and resilience. It is a name that represents the qualities of a strong and powerful woman who is a daughter of God

historical_references.reference: The legend of Saint Viola of Verona tells of a noblewoman who, with her seven handmaidens, was martyred in the late 3rd or early 4th century AD during the Roman persecution of Christians. The group was disguised as men to attend Mass and was betrayed by a pagan priest, leading to their execution.

Another Saint Viola, also known as Violante, is believed to have lived in the 15th century in the Kingdom of Naples. She was a Franciscan tertiary and is venerated as a patron saint of difficult pregnancies and deliveries.
